title: Duryodhana (The Broken Thighs)
body:
Duryodhana (The Broken Thighs)

न हि कल्याणी मतिः कस्यचिद्विनाशाभिमुखे जायते ॥

Translation: No auspicious thoughts arise in the mind of a person who is headed toward destruction. (Mahabharata)

On the eighteenth and final day of the Kurukshetra War, King Shalya took command of the Kuru forces, fighting with monumental valor until Yudhishthira—displaying an uncharacteristic, blazing wrath—hurled a divine spear that pierced Shalya's chest, laying him lifeless on the field. Sahadeva pursued and severed the head of Shakuni, the wicked architect of the dynasty's ruin, while Bhima systematically hunted down and crushed the remaining sons of Dhritarashtra.
Left entirely alone, his eleven Akshauhinis reduced to dust, the wounded and burning Duryodhana walked to the Brahmasarovara lake in the heart of Kurukshetra. Utilizing his magical powers, he entered the waters, cooling his feverish frame and sitting at the bottom of the lake in a yogic trance. The Pandavas, guided by Sree Krishna, tracked him to the pool. Yudhishthira taunted him, demanding if a proud Kshatriya prince would hide himself in a pond like a common fugitive, prompting Duryodhana to rise from the waters, mace in hand, ready to face them all.
Duryodhana engaged Bhima in a final, brutal mace duel. As the two mighty pupils of Balarama clashed, Balarama himself returned from his holy pilgrimage (Theertha-Yatra) to witness the combat. Duryodhana's body, fortified by Gandhari's protective glance, remained completely impervious to Bhima's devastating blows, and he gradually began to overpower the exhausted Pandava. Sree Krishna, watching the crisis, casually tapped His own thigh, signaling to Arjuna to alert Bhima.
Bhima caught the signal, and executing a swift, powerful maneuver, bypassed Duryodhana's guard and shattered his thighs with a crushing blow of his mace. Duryodhana collapsed to the earth, screaming in excruciating agony, his spine shattered. Balarama raged in fury at this flagrant, unlawful breach of the laws of mace combat, which strictly prohibited striking below the navel, and raised his plough to destroy Bhima, until Sree Krishna intervened, placating him by explaining the cosmic necessity of the act and the fulfillment of Bhima's ancient vow at the game of dice. Disgusted by the unclean victory, Balarama departed for Dwaraka, leaving the Pandavas to contemplate the dark, painful transition into the Kali Yuga.
